messages:
IncidentBot: Pager: model warmup failures + node restarts in us-east-2. Symptoms: GPU OOM at load, 'EOF while reading file' deserial errors, repeated container crashloop. Severity: P1 -> paging the on-call rotation.
Sam (on-call): taking. seeing alerts for model=redwood-13b-quant-flash on pool=pool-us-east-2a. ~25% of warmup pods failed last 12m. Customers behind this pool: zenhealth, cloudforms. Any immediate customer impact?
Isha (cust-succ): Zenhealth reports intermittent 502s and slower memos. Cloudforms reports timeouts in batching jobs. I've told them we're investigating.
Rina (eng-runtime): logs show two classes: 1) GPU allocation failures: "cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory" and 2) torch deserialization EOFError: "EOFError: Ran out of memory while unpickling an object". Also seeing: "Worker crashed with signal SIGABRT" from warmup container.
Luca (sre): nodes flapping: k8s node gpu-uste2-7 restarted 3x in 20m. dmesg shows oom_killer targeted /usr/bin/python. kernel memory pressure high.
Sam (on-call): priority actions: - disable warmups for redwood-13b-quant-flash in us-east-2 - cordon problematic node - route incoming traffic away from affected pool (failover to pool-us-east-1) - collect logs/dumps and open incident ticket. I'll run the API calls.
Sam (on-call): POST /internal/warmup/disable?model=redwood-13b-quant-flash&region=us-east-2 -> accepted. WarmupService: disabled warmup for redwood-13b-quant-flash in us-east-2 (actor=sam_oncall).
Sam (on-call): cordoning node: `kubectl cordon gpu-uste2-7` and draining.
Luca (sre): draining. note: several pods with emptyDir volumes may be deleted; warmup pods will be rescheduled. Starting replacement node as well.
Rina (eng-runtime): quick diagnostic: increased compile queue depth due to concurrent warmups and low compile-cache hit rate for this model version. TVM compile worker logs show timeouts: `error: kernel compile exceeded 90s` which blocks resources. Suggest reducing warmup concurrency and forcing precompiled artifacts if available.
Sam (on-call): lowering warmup concurrency for pool to 1. Applying config patch: `set env WARMUP_CONCURRENCY=1` for warmup deployment.
DeployBot: Config patch applied to runtime-warmup (WARMUP_CONCURRENCY=1) - deploy id dpl-20260315-21.
Rina (eng-runtime): also enabling fallback routing: app requests for redwood-13b-quant-flash -> redirect to redwood-7b-quantized when load > 80% or warmup disabled. Pushing routing rule now.
WarmupService: routing rule applied: model fallback configured -> redwood-7b-quantized.
Kayla (support): notified Zenhealth & Cloudforms with ETA: containment in 15-30m, full recovery TBD depending on compile-cache warmup. They've acknowledged.
Sam (on-call): collecting debug logs from one crashed warmup pod:
```
[2026-03-15T22:12:01Z] starting warmup for redwood-13b-quant-flash
[2026-03-15T22:12:05Z] allocating GPU tensors
E cuMemAlloc: failed to allocate 8.3 GiB
E Traceback (most recent call last):
E   File "load_model.py", line 198, in load
E     state = torch.load(f, map_location='cuda')
E EOFError: Ran out of memory while deserializing
[2026-03-15T22:12:07Z] worker exiting with status 134
```
Rina (eng-runtime): additional observation: the model artifact uploaded yesterday has a different checkpoint sharding layout which causes larger peak GPU memory during deserialization. Also the artifact lacked precompiled kernel bundles; that triggered on-host compilation for many kernels. When combined with multiple concurrent warmups on the pool, the host ended up OOMing.
Luca (sre): node replaced -> gpu-uste2-7 -> gpu-uste2-9. New node healthy, no oom_killer events so far.
Sam (on-call): re-enable a canary warmup but force precompiled artifact and concurrency=1. Rina, can you start a canary on gpu-uste2-9?
Rina (eng-runtime): launching canary warmup with env FORCE_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 and WARMUP_CONCURRENCY=1. Monitoring logs.
WarmupService: canary warmup started on gpu-uste2-9/shard-0.
Rina (eng-runtime): canary logs show precompiled kernels loaded, compile queue length=0, torch.load succeeded, peak GPU mem 40.7 GiB within limit. Warmup success. compile cache hit rate for canary=78%.
Sam (on-call): good. rolling re-enable warmup gradually with the new settings. Keep concurrency=1 for 45m and monitor.
Kayla (support): customers updated: Zenhealth reported errors dropped to 1%, Cloudforms report queue backlog reduced. Both appreciate the fast update.
Rina (eng-runtime): immediate follow-ups: 1) add artifact validation that simulates deserialization peak memory snapshot pre-deploy, 2) ensure model artifacts include precompiled kernel bundles when possible, 3) implement warmup rate-limits per-pool and per-model, 4) improve compile-cache telemetry/alerts.
Luca (sre): infra follow-ups: tune host OOM alerts to trigger earlier, prevent concurrent large warmups on same AZ if host driver updates pending. Filed INFRA-20260315-11.
Sam (on-call): creating incident ticket INC-20260315-87 and assigning owners: Rina for runtime fixes, Luca for infra tuning, Isha for customer comms. Postmortem draft due EOD tomorrow.
IncidentBot: severity downgraded to P2. Reminder set for postmortem in 24h.
Sam (on-call): saving logs, heap-dumps, nvidia-smi outputs to s3://redwood-incidents/1919991234/ for 30d retention.
Isha (cust-succ): following up with customers and scheduling a sync with Zenhealth engineering tomorrow.
Rina (eng-runtime): taking action items and will draft timeline + technical RCA. Adding myself to customer threads if needed.
Sam (on-call): handing off to Rina for post-incident actions. I'm out for the next 3 hours. Thanks all. :wave:
